proposed_reports.title: City of Winnipeg Multi-Year Budget — 2026 Update (Operating, Reserves and Capital)
proposed_reports.description: Annual update to the 2024-2027 multi-year operating, reserves and capital budget. 2026 edition sets a 3.5% municipal property tax increase (mill rate 13.372) dedicated partly to roads and tax-supported operations; total City revenue approximately $2.5 billion.

proposed_reports.title: Real and Personal Property Municipal Tax Rate By-law (annual)
proposed_reports.description: Annual by-law under The City of Winnipeg Charter s. 334(1) establishing the municipal mill rate on portioned assessment. 2026 mill rate set at 13.372 (3.5% increase from 12.920). Separate from school-division and provincial education-support levies.

proposed_reports.title: City of Winnipeg Annual Financial Report — Consolidated Audited Financial Statements
proposed_reports.description: Annual consolidated audited financial statements prepared under Canadian public sector accounting standards for the year ended 31 December, covering tax-supported operations, utilities and controlled entities. 2025 edition available; 2024 edition also published.

proposed_reports.title: City of Winnipeg Property Assessment Roll / Notices
proposed_reports.publisher: City of Winnipeg Assessment and Taxation Department
proposed_reports.description: Annual (and general reassessment-cycle) market-value assessment of properties within Winnipeg. Portioned at class-specific percentages (residential 45%). 2027 general assessment roll delivery announced for June 2026; City maintains its own assessment function separate from provincial Property Assessment Services.

proposed_reports.title: The Saskatoon Property Tax Bylaw, 2026 (Bylaw No. 10174)
proposed_reports.description: Annual bylaw under The Cities Act authorizing municipal and library mill rates and mill-rate factors against taxable assessments for 2026. Uniform municipal rate 9.1147 mills; residential tax rate 0.0080291 after factors. Passed 29 April 2026.

proposed_reports.title: City of Saskatoon Multi-Year Business Plan and Budget (Operating, Capital & Climate)
proposed_reports.description: Multi-year operating, capital and climate budget approved by Council. 2026/2027 edition incorporates tax-supported revenue share of approximately 51% and rate increases for utilities; taxation remains the largest single revenue source.

proposed_reports.title: City of Saskatoon Annual Report — Consolidated Financial Statements
proposed_reports.description: Annual consolidated financial statements and statistical section prepared under Canadian public sector accounting standards. 2024 edition reports taxation revenue of $347.8 million and total consolidated operating revenues of $1.31 billion.

proposed_reports.title: City of Saskatoon Property Assessment Roll / Notices
proposed_reports.description: Annual assessment notices and public assessment roll prepared under provincial legislation with SAMA oversight. 2025 was a provincially legislated revaluation year (base date 2023); next full revaluation 2029. Supplemental assessments issued for physical changes.

proposed_reports.title: SAMA Municipal Assessment Return (annual form and confirmation process)
proposed_reports.description: Standardised annual return submitted by municipalities to SAMA Quality Assurance for confirmation of the assessment roll. Required under The Assessment Management Agency Act; once confirmed, the roll is valid for tax enforcement. Blank form, checklist and sample published each year; Certificates of Confirmation issued and gazetted.

proposed_reports.title: City of Regina Annual Budget (Operating and Capital)
proposed_reports.description: Annual operating and capital budget adopted under The Cities Act. 2026 edition approved December 2025 with a 10.9% mill-rate increase; focuses on core services, police, fire and infrastructure renewal.

proposed_reports.title: The Regina Property Tax Bylaw (annual)
proposed_reports.description: Annual bylaw establishing municipal, library and school mill rates and mill-rate factors against taxable assessments. 2025 edition (Bylaw 2025-30) available; 2026 rates published on City tax-calculation pages (municipal mill rate factors applied to base rates).

dependencies.basis: Council recommendation explicitly directs enactment of the Real and Personal Property Municipal Tax Rate By-law to raise the revenue required by the approved operating budget, setting the mill rate from the budget-determined levy.
dependencies.evidence_quote: That the City’s mill rate be increased from 12.920 to 13.372 for 2026, for the purpose of raising revenue as required for the annual operating budget and that Council enact a Real and Personal Property Municipal Tax Rate By-law for 2026 for this purpose in accordance with subsection 334(1) of The City of Winnipeg Charter.
